schema.label: LUNGMAP registration
schema.text: Three entry routes: pre-screening before progression on current therapy (tissue only), screening at progression (tissue or prior NGS results), or treatment-naive NSCLC with a designated targetable alteration (prior NGS results only, when such sub-studies are open).

schema.label: Biomarker profiling
schema.text: Tissue sent to Foundation Medicine within 5 days of registration for broad CLIA NGS profiling, or upload of a previously completed approved NGS report via the Genomic Alterations Form.

schema.label: Sub-study assignment
schema.text: Biomarker-matched sub-study if a qualifying alteration is found (lowest prevalence or randomized assignment if several match); otherwise a non-match sub-study if one is accruing. Assignment within about 16 days of tissue submission, within 1 day for prior test results; pre-screened patients receive assignment after the Notice of Progression is submitted.

schema.label: Sub-study registration
schema.text: Separate registration to the assigned sub-study, which has its own eligibility and treatment. After progression on a sub-study, a new assignment may be requested.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until sub-study registration, death, or 3 years after LUNGMAP registration; after sub-study registration, until death or 3 years.

schema.label: Primary objective
schema.text: Screening protocol: determine eligibility for the biomarker-driven and non-match Lung-MAP sub-studies.

eligibility: Pathologically or cytologically proven NSCLC; mixed NSCLC histologies allowed, but no known small cell component.
Stage IV, or recurrent or progressive NSCLC without a curative treatment option (staging per AJCC 7th edition or later).
Age ≥ 18; Zubrod/ECOG performance status 0-2 documented within 28 days before registration.

Pre-screening: tissue available for on-study profiling; currently on, or previously received, first-line standard therapy for stage IV or recurrent disease and not yet progressed on the current or most recent line. Patients using prior biomarker results cannot be pre-screened. Patients on osimertinib aiming for S1900G must not be pre-screened.

Screening at progression: at least one prior line of standard systemic therapy for stage I-IV NSCLC with progression during or after the most recent line. If no prior therapy for stage IV or recurrent disease, progression must have occurred ≤ 180 days after the last dose of stage I-III systemic therapy; if > 180 days, standard therapy for advanced disease and progression on it are required first.

Screening at progression biomarker route: tissue for on-study profiling, an approved prior NGS report, or a non-listed NGS report (or specific biomarker documentation) accepted by e-mail from LUNGMAPNGS@swog.org. For EGFR-mutant, MET-amplified disease screening for S1900G, tissue must be obtained after progression on osimertinib.

Treatment-naive route: no prior systemic therapy for stage IV or recurrent NSCLC and documentation (approved or e-mail-accepted NGS report) of a biomarker for a sub-study open to treatment-naive patients. Do not submit tissue for this route.

Tissue for on-study testing: FFPE block, or 12 unstained slides plus an H&E (or 13 unstained slides) at 4-5 microns, with ≥ 20% tumor cells and ≥ 0.2 mm3 tumor volume; no decalcified bone biopsies (cell blocks of pleural fluid acceptable). Consent to Foundation Medicine testing and banking of leftover tissue.

Prior test reports: full report available, tissue or blood specified, original report dated on or after September 1, 2019, from a CLIA/CAP/ISO-certified lab (non-listed tests need gene list and e-mail approval). A blood-only NGS report must show at least one alteration on the Genomic Alterations Form, otherwise tissue testing is required.

When the patient goes to surgery, the adenocarcinoma that is removed is tested again. The results of that test are used to guide the choice of therapy after surgery. arms.text: The standard of care can consist of surveillance (which means the continuation of the ongoing systemic treatment without any change) or initiation of NEST. Subjects who fulfil all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria will be enrolled and receive treatment with Durvalumab and EP for 4 cycles. Durvalumab will be administered at a dose of 1500 mg every 3 weeks (Q3W) with first-line chemotherapy and will continue to be administered as monotherapy every 4 weeks(Q4W) post-chemotherapy until progressive disease. The LDRT deals with primary tumour in a 15 Gy of 5 fractions over five days, starting from Day 1 in the first cycle. Subjects will attend safety follow up 12 weeks ±14 days after last dose of Durvalumab. The primary endpoint is mPFS.
